annotations.derivable_answer: Highly edit-robust LLM watermarks are vulnerable to piggyback spoofing, where an adversary alters critical content while the watermark retains attribution. The Cocktail watermarking scheme resolves this by co-embedding a robust signal and a fragile signal into each generated token; they share the same mechanism but use independent keys and different seeding windows over normalized text, producing a two-dimensional score space that supports three decisions: Intact, Tampered, and No-Watermark.

annotations.derivable_answer: Strategic drift in LLM agents during long-horizon reasoning tasks is primarily caused by inconsistent subgoals due to finite attention resources preventing the model from maintaining strategic coherence over thousands of steps. annotations.derivable_answer: In AI-generated fiction, 'formal range' specifically means the dispersion and coordination among measured stylistic features (not narrative structure). 'Overclosure' describes a corpus-level condition where generated texts remain locally fluent and coherent but exhibit an unusually restricted tendency across measured formal dimensions. 'Variance overclosure' means novels differ very little from one another across individual features (lexical diversity, sentence length, readability), whereas 'correlational overclosure' is an exploratory hypothesis that features not mechanically related become more strongly coordinated across texts than in human comparators. They differ because a corpus can be variance-restricted without its variables becoming interdependent, or vice versa.

when we say “formal
range,” we specifically mean the dispersion and
coordination among the stylistic features we have
measured; we do not mean plot, characterization,
point of view, or overall narrative structure.

Overclosure describes a corpus-level condition
in which generated texts remain locally fluent and
coherent but depict an unusually restricted tendency across the measured formal dimensions.

“Variance over closure” means that novels differ
very little from one another with respect to fea2
tures such as lexical diversity, entropy, sentence
length, or readability.

“Correlational over closure”
is an exploratory hypothesis concerning features

strongly coordinated in generated texts than in a
human comparator.

These two types of over closure differ from one
another: a corpus can be restricted without its variables becoming interdependent, or conversely, its
variables can become interdependent without all of
them being compressed to the same degree.

annotations.derivable_answer: Prior prototype-based detectors learn class anchors as independent entities from support examples without constraining the relational geometry among the prototypes themselves. Class-Geometry Supervision (CGS) structurally departs from this by explicitly supervising the prototype space using known class relationships, aligning pairwise prototype distances with a target class-geometry matrix estimated from training data. Ablations reveal that meaningful visual geometry provides the most reliable gains, whereas random geometry can aid novel class separation but is less consistent for few-shot detection.

annotations.derivable_answer: In AI-generated fiction, 'formal range' specifically means the dispersion and coordination among measured stylistic features (not plot or characterization). 'Overclosure' describes a corpus-level condition where generated texts remain locally fluent and coherent but exhibit an unusually restricted tendency across measured formal dimensions. 'Variance overclosure' means novels differ very little from one another across individual features (lexical diversity, sentence length, readability), whereas 'correlational overclosure' is an exploratory hypothesis that features not mechanically related become more strongly coordinated across texts than in human comparators. They differ because variable interdependence and variance restriction can occur independently.
